proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(G=G_P\) and \(Q=Q_P=\operatorname{adj}G\).  The trace pairing on \(S3\) is nondegenerate.  Because \(G\) is the gradient of \(P\), equality of the two second directional derivatives gives, for all \(H,J\in S3\),
\[
 \operatorname{tr}\!\left(\mathrm dG_X(H)J\right)
 =\mathrm d^2P_X(H,J)
 =\mathrm d^2P_X(J,H)
 =\operatorname{tr}\!\left(H\,\mathrm dG_X(J)\right).
\]
This identity uses the trace-pairing definition of \(G_P\); in ordinary coordinates it is exactly the convention that an off-diagonal coordinate derivative is twice the corresponding off-diagonal entry of \(G_P\).

Expanding the determinant by the Leibniz formula and differentiating each monomial shows, including at singular matrices, that its directional derivative at a matrix \(A\) in direction \(B\) is \(\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(A)B)\).  Applying this identity and the hypothesis \(\det G\equiv0\) gives, for arbitrary \(H\in S3\),
\[
 0=\mathrm d(\det G)_X(H)
  =\operatorname{tr}\!\left(Q(X)\,\mathrm dG_X(H)\right)
  =\operatorname{tr}\!\left(\mathrm dG_X(Q(X))H\right).
\]
Nondegeneracy of the trace pairing therefore gives
\[
 \mathrm dG_X(Q(X))=0. \tag{1}
\]
Let \(\mathcal L\) be the polynomial derivation \(\mathcal Lh(X)=\mathrm dh_X(Q(X))\), acting entrywise on matrix-valued polynomials.  Equation (1), the polynomial chain rule for the adjugate, and \(GQ=(\det G)I_3\) give
\[
 \mathcal LG=0,
 \qquad
 \mathcal LQ=\mathrm d(\operatorname{adj})_{G}(\mathcal LG)=0,
 \qquad
 \mathcal LP=\operatorname{tr}(GQ)=3\det G=0. \tag{2}
\]
For every scalar polynomial \(h\) and every integer \(k\geq0\), induction using \(\mathcal LQ=0\) yields
\[
 \mathcal L^kh(X)=\mathrm d^kh_X\bigl(Q(X),\ldots,Q(X)\bigr). \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, differentiating the right side along \(Q(X)\) gives its next directional derivative plus \(k\) terms containing \(\mathrm dQ_X(Q(X))=\mathcal LQ(X)=0\).  Apply (3) entrywise first to \(G\), and then to \(Q=\operatorname{adj}G\), or apply it directly with (2).  Since every derivative of order exceeding the polynomial degree vanishes, the finite Taylor formula and (2)--(3) give
\[
 G(X+tQ(X))=G(X),
 \qquad
 Q(X+tQ(X))=Q(X),
 \qquad
 P(X+tQ(X))=P(X)
\]
for every \(X\in S3\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\).  These are precisely the asserted identities for \(\mathcal T_P\).

Write \(G=G_P\).  We first derive monotonicity from the positive-semidefinite gradient hypothesis.  If \(A,B\in C3\) and \(B-A\succeq0\), convexity of \(C3\) and the fundamental theorem of calculus give
\[
 P(B)-P(A)
 =\int_0^1\operatorname{tr}\!\left(G(A+s(B-A))(B-A)\right)\,\mathrm ds\geq0. \tag{4}
\]
The last inequality holds because the trace of the product of two positive-semidefinite symmetric matrices is nonnegative.

Choose \(X_0\in C3\) with \(\operatorname{rank}G(X_0)=2\).  Since \(G(X_0)\succeq0\), its two nonzero eigenvalues are positive.  Consequently
\[
 Q_P(X_0)=\operatorname{adj}G(X_0)=\kappa uu^{\top}
\]
for some \(\kappa>0\) and some \(u\neq0\) spanning \(\ker G(X_0)\).  The adjugate-translation lemma, followed by rescaling its scalar parameter by \(\kappa\), gives
\[
 P(X_0+tuu^{\top})=P(X_0) \qquad(t\in\mathbb R). \tag{5}
\]

Fix arbitrary \(X\in C3\).  Because \(X_0\succ0\), there is \(R>0\) such that \(X\preceq RX_0\); for example, any \(R\) not smaller than the largest eigenvalue of \(X_0^{-1/2}XX_0^{-1/2}\) works.  For every \(t\geq0\), all matrices in the following comparison are positive definite.  Applying (4), homogeneity of degree \(r\), and (5), in that order, gives the two-sided bound
\[
 P(X)
 \leq P(X+tuu^{\top})
 \leq P(RX_0+tuu^{\top})
 =R^rP\!\left(X_0+\frac{t}{R}uu^{\top}\right)
 =R^rP(X_0). \tag{6}
\]
Thus the real polynomial \(t\mapsto P(X+tuu^{\top})\) is bounded above and below on \([0,\infty)\).  A nonconstant real polynomial is unbounded in absolute value on that half-line, so this polynomial is constant.  Differentiating at \(t=0\) gives
\[
 u^{\top}G(X)u=0.
\]
Since \(G(X)\succeq0\), the spectral theorem implies \(G(X)u=0\).  This holds for every \(X\in C3\).  Each coordinate of the vector-valued polynomial \(G(X)u\) vanishes on the nonempty open set \(C3\), hence vanishes identically on \(S3\).

Finally choose an invertible, and in fact orthogonal, change of coordinates carrying \(u\) to a nonzero multiple of the third coordinate vector.  Then \(G(X)u=0\) says that the derivatives of \(P\) with respect to \(x_{13},x_{23},x_{33}\) vanish; the off-diagonal equalities use the half-weighted gradient convention.  A polynomial with these three zero partial derivatives depends only on \(x_{11},x_{12},x_{22}\), namely on the symmetric compression of \(X\) to \(u^{\perp}\).  This proves both conclusions.

The cited three-dimensional reduction supplies the mixed-branch hypotheses appearing in the statement; the remaining assertions are derived here.  Maximal divisibility \(D=\delta^eE\), homogeneity of \(D\) of degree \(K\), and homogeneity of \(\delta\) of degree three imply that \(E\), and hence \(F=sE\), is homogeneous of degree
\[
 L=K-3e.
\]
The cone \(C3\) is connected, \(E\) is continuous, and the mixed-branch premise says that \(E\) has no zero on \(C3\).  Therefore \(E\) has constant sign there.  Since \(s=\operatorname{sign}E(I3)\),
\[
 F(X)=sE(X)>0 \qquad(X\in C3). \tag{7}
\]
Euler's identity under the trace-pairing gradient convention is
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(G_E(X)X)=L E(X).
\]
Taking the trace of the assumed relative spectrum \(\{a+b,b,0\}\) gives \(L=a+2b\), so in particular \(L\geq1\).

For \(X\in C3\), define the symmetric matrix
\[
 B(X)=\frac{X^{1/2}G_E(X)X^{1/2}}{E(X)}.
\]
It is similar to \(G_E(X)X/E(X)\), because
\[
 B(X)=X^{1/2}\frac{G_E(X)X}{E(X)}X^{-1/2}.
\]
Hence \(B(X)\) has eigenvalues \(a+b,b,0\).  The conditions \(a,b\geq1\) show that \(B(X)\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}B(X)=2\).  Since \(G_F=sG_E\) and \(F=sE\), equation (7) yields the congruence
\[
 G_F(X)=F(X)X^{-1/2}B(X)X^{-1/2}\succeq0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{rank}G_F(X)=2. \tag{8}
\]
Thus \(\det G_F(X)=0\) on the nonempty open set \(C3\).  Because \(\det G_F\) is a polynomial on \(S3\), polynomial continuation gives \(\det G_F\equiv0\) on \(S3\).  Equations (7)--(8), together with the homogeneity calculation, prove every assertion.

Assume first the self-normalization identity with \(c>0\).  The three algebraic assumptions place \(D\) in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{SN},3}\).  Apply the cited Tamano three-dimensional reduction after writing \(D=\delta^eE\) with maximal \(e\).  Its constant, line, and plane branches already have respectively the forms \(\lambda_0\delta^e\), \(\lambda_0\Delta_1^a\delta^e\), and \(\lambda_0\Delta_2^b\delta^e\), with the unused member of the flag chosen arbitrarily so as to obtain \(V1\subset V2\).

It remains to treat the mixed branch.  The cited reduction supplies integers \(a,b\geq1\), interior nonvanishing, and
\[
 \operatorname{spec}\!\left(\frac{G_E(X)X}{E(X)}\right)=\{a+b,b,0\}
 \qquad(X\in C3). \tag{9}
\]
The mixed-residue bridge shows that the signed residue \(F=sE\) is homogeneous and that \(G_F\) is positive semidefinite of rank two on \(C3\), with \(\det G_F\equiv0\).  The positive-gradient kernel-rigidity theorem therefore provides a fixed \(u\neq0\) with \(G_F(X)u=0\) identically.  After an orthogonal change of coordinates taking \(u\) to the third coordinate direction, \(F\) is a polynomial \(f\) of the leading \(2\times2\) symmetric compression.

For a positive-definite \(2\times2\) matrix \(Y\), insert \(X=\operatorname{diag}(Y,z)\) with \(z>0\).  Because \(G_FX/F\) has the spectrum in (9),
\[
 2\operatorname{tr}\{(G_F(X)X)^2\}
 =2\bigl((a+b)^2+b^2\bigr)F(X)^2
\]
on \(C3\), and hence identically by polynomial continuation.  The zero third row and column of \(G_F(X)\) now show that \(f\) satisfies the corresponding two-dimensional exact self-normalization identity.  The cited two-dimensional converse then gives
\[
 f(Y)=\lambda_0\det(CYC^{\top})^a\det(Y)^b
\]
for a nonzero row vector \(C\), after relabeling its line exponent and determinant exponent.  These exponents are indeed the same \(a,b\) as in (9), because the ordered relative eigenvalues of this two-dimensional flag power are \(a+b,b\).  Returning to the original coordinates identifies \(V2=u^{\perp}\) and a line \(V1\subset V2\), and restoring the stripped determinant gives
\[
 D(X)=\lambda_0\Delta_1(X)^a\Delta_2(X)^b\delta(X)^e.
\]

Conversely, the cited flag-sufficiency theorem applies to every such nested flag form and gives
\[
 2\operatorname{tr}\{(G_D(X)X)^2\}
 =2\bigl((a+b+e)^2+(b+e)^2+e^2\bigr)D(X)^2. \tag{10}
\]
The positive sum condition makes \(D\) nonconstant, and the displayed constant is positive.  Since \(D^2\not\equiv0\), comparison with the assumed identity also shows that the value of \(c\) is forced to be the value in (10).

For completeness, active-flag uniqueness is algebraic.  The coordinate ring of \(S3\) is a unique-factorization domain.  After an invertible congruence change of variables, a line minor is a nonzero scalar multiple of \(x_{11}\), a plane minor is a nonzero scalar multiple of \(x_{11}x_{22}-x_{12}^2\), and the full determinant is \(\delta\).  The first two are irreducible.  To see irreducibility of \(\delta\), regard it as a degree-one polynomial in \(x_{33}\).  A proper factor independent of \(x_{33}\) would divide both its coefficient \(x_{11}x_{22}-x_{12}^2\) and its constant term, but the irreducible coefficient does not divide that constant term, as is seen on the specialization \(x_{11}=1,x_{12}=x_{22}=0\).  Thus \(\delta\) is irreducible as well.  Unique factorization identifies every active factor up to a nonzero scalar.  Associate line minors have proportional rank-one coefficient matrices and hence the same line.  Writing a plane minor, up to a nonzero scalar, as \(v^{\top}\operatorname{adj}(X)v\), associate plane minors have proportional matrices \(vv^{\top}\) and hence the same orthogonal-complement line, so they determine the same plane.  Therefore every subspace whose exponent is positive is unique; an inactive subspace is, correctly, not asserted to be unique.

All initial operations in \(\mathcal A_D\) are finite exact operations on rational coefficient arrays.  After the zero, constant, and homogeneity guards, put
\[
 T=2\operatorname{tr}\{(G_DX)^2\},
 \qquad
 R=D^2.
\]
Choose a monomial whose coefficient \(p\) in \(R\) is nonzero, and let \(t\) be its coefficient in \(T\).  If \(T=cR\) for any scalar \(c\), coefficient comparison forces \(c=c_0=t/p\).  Hence \(c_0\leq0\) is an exact rejection witness, while for \(c_0>0\) any nonzero coefficient of \(T-c_0R\) is an exact rejection witness.  If the residual is zero, the guarded polynomial belongs to \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{SN},3}\), and the complete classification applies.

For a classified polynomial every compression determinant is positive at \(I3\), so \(D(I3)\neq0\); thus the identity test can never lead a member to fail the next guard.  Conversely, if the guard \(D(I3)=0\) fires, the classification shows that the input cannot be a member.  It is therefore safe to form the rational symmetric matrix
\[
 J_D=\frac{G_D(I3)}{D(I3)}.
\]
For any full-row-rank basis matrix \(B\), differentiation at \(I3\) gives
\[
 G_{\log\det(BXB^{\top})}(I3)
 =B^{\top}(BB^{\top})^{-1}B=\Pi_{\operatorname{row}(B)}, \tag{11}
\]
the orthogonal projection onto its row space.  Therefore a flag form satisfies
\[
 J_D=a\Pi_{V1}+b\Pi_{V2}+eI_3. \tag{12}
\]
Nested orthogonal projections commute.  On the orthogonal decomposition
\[
 \mathbb R^3=V1\oplus(V2\cap V1^{\perp})\oplus V2^{\perp},
\]
equation (12) has the ordered eigenvalues
\[
 \lambda_1=a+b+e,
 \qquad
 \lambda_2=b+e,
 \qquad
 \lambda_3=e. \tag{13}
\]
Consequently the recognizer recovers
\[
 a=\lambda_1-\lambda_2,
 \qquad
 b=\lambda_2-\lambda_3,
 \qquad
 e=\lambda_3. \tag{14}
\]
These numbers are nonnegative integers on every accepted input.  Because \(J_D\) is rational and the eigenvalues in (13) are integers, the relevant eigenspaces are rational nullspaces.  Exact Gaussian elimination therefore returns rational bases for every active space.  If \(a=0\), a rational line may be chosen inside the recovered plane; if \(b=0\), a rational plane may be chosen containing the recovered line; if \(a=b=0\), any rational complete flag may be chosen.  These choices affect only inactive flag entries.

For the recovered rational bases define
\[
 \lambda_0=
 \frac{D(I3)}{\Delta_1(I3)^a\Delta_2(I3)^b},
\]
where \(\delta(I3)^e=1\).  This is a nonzero rational number.  Exact expansion of \(D-D_{\mathrm{flag}}\) verifies every coefficient.  The classification and the active-space uniqueness just proved show that this residual is zero for every member.  Conversely, a zero residual directly verifies the flag form and hence, by flag sufficiency, membership; thus no false acceptance is possible.  Formula (10) gives
\[
 c=2\bigl(\lambda_1^2+\lambda_2^2+\lambda_3^2\bigr).
\]
Every branch of the procedure consists of differentiation, arithmetic on finitely many rational coefficients, factorization of a cubic characteristic polynomial, rational nullspace computation, and finite coefficient comparison.  Hence it terminates.  The failed guard or coefficient, or else the data in (13)--(14), the rational bases, \(\lambda_0\), \(c\), and the zero residual, is exactly the asserted certificate.  No estimate of bit complexity was used.

added_lemmas.statement:
For a nested flag \(V1\subset V2\), full-row-rank bases \(B1,B2\), nonnegative integers \(a,b,e\) with \(a+b+e>0\), and \(\lambda_0\neq0\), the polynomial \(D_{\mathrm{flag}}=\lambda_0\Delta_1^a\Delta_2^b\delta^e\) satisfies
\[
 2\operatorname{tr}\{(G_{D_{\mathrm{flag}}}(X)X)^2\}
 =2\bigl((a+b+e)^2+(b+e)^2+e^2\bigr)D_{\mathrm{flag}}(X)^2
\]
identically on \(S3\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(p\) be a nonzero, nonconstant homogeneous polynomial on \(\operatorname{Sym}_{2}(\mathbb R)\).  If for some \(c_2>0\) its trace-pairing symmetric gradient \(G_p\) satisfies
\[
 2\operatorname{tr}\{(G_p(Y)Y)^2\}=c_2p(Y)^2
\]
identically, then there are a line \(W1\subset\mathbb R^2\), integers \(j,k\geq0\) with \(j+k>0\), and \(\rho\neq0\) such that
\[
 p(Y)=\rho\det(C1YC1^{\top})^j\det(Y)^k,
\]
where \(C1\) is any full-row-rank basis of \(W1\).  When \(j>0\), the line \(W1\) is unique.

For \(D\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{SN},3}\), write \(D=\delta^eE\) with \(e\) maximal.  Tamano's three-dimensional determinant-stripping and spectral reduction classifies the constant, rank-one, and pure-plane residue branches as flag powers.  In the remaining mixed branch, \(E\) is nonzero on \(C3\), and there are integers \(a,b\geq1\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{spec}\!\left(\frac{G_E(X)X}{E(X)}\right)=\{a+b,b,0\}
 \qquad(X\in C3).
\]
In this mixed branch, constancy of the one-dimensional kernel of \(G_E(X)\) reduces the residue to the two-dimensional converse and is the only unresolved step in that reduction.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(d\geq2\), and let \(D_d\) be a homogeneous polynomial of positive degree on \(Sd=\operatorname{Sym}_{d}(\mathbb R)\), with trace-pairing symmetric gradient \(G_{D_d}\).  If \(G_{D_d}(X)\succeq0\) for every \(X\in\mathbb S_{++}^{d}\), \(\det G_{D_d}\equiv0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}G_{D_d}(X_0)=d-1\) for some \(X_0\in\mathbb S_{++}^{d}\), then there is \(u\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(G_{D_d}(X)u=0\) identically on \(Sd\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(G=G_{D_d}\), \(Q=\operatorname{adj}G\), and let the homogeneous degree be \(k\geq1\).  Hessian symmetry for the trace pairing and differentiation of \(\det G\equiv0\) give
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(\mathrm dG_X(Q(X))H)
 =\operatorname{tr}(Q(X)\mathrm dG_X(H))
 =\mathrm d(\det G)_X(H)=0
\]
for every symmetric \(H\), hence \(\mathrm dG_X(Q(X))=0\).  Therefore the polynomial derivation \(\mathcal Lh=\mathrm dh(Q)\) annihilates \(G\), \(Q\), and
\[
 \mathcal LD_d=\operatorname{tr}(GQ)=d\det G=0.
\]
The same finite Taylor induction as in the three-dimensional adjugate-translation lemma yields
\[
 D_d(X+tQ(X))=D_d(X) \qquad(t\in\mathbb R). \tag{16}
\]
At \(X_0\), positive semidefiniteness and rank \(d-1\) imply \(Q(X_0)=\kappa uu^{\top}\) for some \(\kappa>0\) and \(u\neq0\).  Hence (16) is invariance along \(uu^{\top}\).  For arbitrary \(X\succ0\), choose \(R>0\) with \(X\preceq RX_0\).  Gradient positivity gives cone monotonicity, and for \(t\geq0\) it yields
\[
 D_d(X)
 \leq D_d(X+tuu^{\top})
 \leq D_d(RX_0+tuu^{\top})
 =R^kD_d(X_0).
\]
The middle expression is a polynomial in \(t\), bounded above and below on \([0,\infty)\), and is therefore constant.  Thus \(u^{\top}G(X)u=0\), and positive semidefiniteness gives \(G(X)u=0\) on the positive-definite cone.  Polynomial continuation proves the identity on all of \(Sd\).

proposed.statement:
Let \(D\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{SN},3}\), construct \(E,s,F\) using the signed determinant-free mixed-residue definition, and suppose Tamano's determinant-stripped reduction places \(E\) in the mixed branch: \(E(X)\neq0\) on \(C3\), and for some integers \(a,b\geq1\),
\[
 \operatorname{spec}\!\left(\frac{G_E(X)X}{E(X)}\right)=\{a+b,b,0\}
\]
for every \(X\in C3\).  Then \(F(tX)=t^LF(X)\) with \(L=K-3e\geq1\), \(F(X)>0\) and \(G_F(X)\succeq0\) for every \(X\in C3\), \(\det G_F\equiv0\) in \(\mathbb R[S3]\), and \(\operatorname{rank}G_F(X)=2\) for every \(X\in C3\).
proposed.justification: Sign normalization and the congruence of the symmetric relative gradient derive exactly the positivity, determinant-singularity, and rank hypotheses used by kernel rigidity.
proposed.gap: Tamano's determinant stripping and spectral reduction establish interior nonvanishing and the mixed relative spectrum; this bridge transfers those conclusions to the half-weighted symmetric gradient.
proposed.consumer: The complete classification invokes kernel rigidity for the actual signed mixed residue.

proposed.statement:
Let \(D\) be nonzero, nonconstant, and homogeneous of degree \(K\).  The identity
\[
 2\operatorname{tr}\{(G_D(X)X)^2\}=cD(X)^2
\]
holds on \(S3\) for some \(c>0\) if and only if there exist \(V1\subset V2\), \(a,b,e\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\) with \(a+b+e>0\), and \(\lambda_0\neq0\) such that \(D=D_{\mathrm{flag}}\).  In that representation,
\[
 c=2\bigl((a+b+e)^2+(b+e)^2+e^2\bigr),
\]
and every flag subspace whose corresponding exponent is positive is unique.
proposed.justification: This degree-unrestricted converse is the algebraic engine for a complete audit of reduced three-variable rational causal denominators.
proposed.gap: Tamano supplies flag sufficiency, determinant stripping, spectral reduction, the dimension-two converse, and the pure branches; positive-gradient kernel rigidity closes the remaining mixed kernel-line branch.
proposed.consumer: The reduced-denominator audit turns the classification into an if-and-only-if certificate for primitive rational covariance formulas.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the cited flag sufficiency, dimension-two converse, and three-dimensional reduction used by the proof, and reflow the same claim with compilable TeX.

proposed.statement:
Let \(\tau(\Sigma)=N(\Sigma)/D(\Sigma)\) be an upstream-valid primitive coprime reduced rational causal certificate, obtained for example by the half-trek criterion, supported on \(S3\), with \(D\) nonzero, nonconstant, and homogeneous.  Its denominator is exactly self-normalizing if and only if
\[
 D=\lambda_0\Delta_1^a\Delta_2^b\delta^e
\]
for one nested flag and nonnegative integers \(a,b,e\) with positive sum.  If the coefficients are rational, \(\mathcal A_D\) decides this property from the primitive input.  Under Gaussian sampling,
\[
 \frac{D(\widehat\Sigma)}{D(\Sigma)}
 \stackrel{d}{=}
 \prod_{j=1}^{3}
 \left(\frac{\chi^2_{n-j+1}}{n}\right)^{m_j},
 \qquad
 m=(a+b+e,b+e,e),
\]
with independent factors; consequently \(\Pr_{\Sigma}\{D(\Sigma)\in\mathcal I_D(\eta)\}=1-\eta\).
proposed.justification: This isolates the valid statistical payoff: exhaustive denominator classification plus the known exact pivot for the denominator value.
proposed.gap: Half-trek theory can produce rational identifying functionals, while Tamano's pivot applies to known flag powers; the new converse makes applicability decidable for every qualifying reduced three-variable denominator.
proposed.consumer: Analysts can attach an exact confidence set to the denominator value while keeping inference for the causal ratio outside the claim.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine whether the self-normalization equations in dimensions at least four force a recursive common invariant flag in every higher-corank branch, or construct and certify a counterexample.
open_obligations.obstruction: When the positive-semidefinite gradient has corank at least two, its adjugate vanishes, so determinant differentiation produces no nonzero translation direction.  Moreover, the first two spectral power sums supplied by homogeneity and self-normalization do not determine a spectrum with four or more entries.
open_obligations.attempted: The adjugate-translation and two-sided cone-order argument was generalized to arbitrary dimension and completely closes the corank-one case.  Direct replacement of the adjugate by lower cofactors was examined, but determinant differentiation does not show that the corresponding lower-cofactor direction is annihilated by the Hessian, so the finite translation step is unavailable.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved all-dimensional corank-one rigidity lemma shows that whenever a candidate branch has \(G_{D_d}\succeq0\), \(\det G_{D_d}\equiv0\), and rank \(d-1\) at one positive-definite point, its kernel line is globally constant.  Thus the higher-dimensional question is closed for the corank-one branch.  The unresolved cases have generic rank at most \(d-2\), where \(\operatorname{adj}G_{D_d}\equiv0\) and the present translation direction disappears.
